# robots.txt for StackEnhance
# https://stackenhance.com
#
# Public: the start pages (/, /se, /signal, /studio and their /se twins), the
# brand directory and brand pages (/brands…, /se/brands…), blog, help,
# pricing and legal.
#
# The logged-in app is listed below so crawlers do not spend time on it. Share
# links, invitations, onboarding and the Studio prospect pages are NOT listed
# on purpose: they carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (vercel.json), and a crawler
# can only read that header on a URL it is allowed to fetch — a disallowed URL
# that someone links can still be indexed by its address alone, which for a
# share link or a prospect page is exactly what must not happen.
#
# Prefix rules: `/signal/` and `/studio/` (trailing slash) leave the public
# /signal and /studio start pages crawlable; `/brand/` (the app) does not match
# the public `/brands/`.

User-agent: *
Allow: /

# API (the brand pages and sitemaps reach crawlers through rewrites, not /api)
Disallow: /api/

# The logged-in app
Disallow: /signal/
Disallow: /admin
Disallow: /dashboard
Disallow: /emails
Disallow: /brand/
Disallow: /campaigns
Disallow: /calendar

Disallow: /resources

# sitemap-index.xml lists sitemap.xml (every public page, generated at build)
# and sitemap-brands.xml (every indexable brand page, from the backend).

www.apier.no:
# Apier.no crawl policy (advisory only; real access control is enforced in the auth layer).
# Public API + agent-discovery surfaces are crawlable; auth-gated /api/ paths stay blocked.
# Allow lines precede Disallow so first-match crawlers permit the public subpaths before
# the broad /api/ block; Google's longest-match resolves the same either way.
User-agent: *
Allow: /api/v1/public/
Allow: /api/v1/sandbox/public/
Allow: /api/v1/tools/
Allow: /api/v1/capabilities
Allow: /api/v1/pricing
Allow: /api/v1/comparison/
Allow: /.well-known/
# Discovery reads that llms.txt advertises: agents and AI crawlers may fetch
# them. /api/v1/sandbox/fixtures, /api/v1/errors and /api/mcp answer with
# X-Robots-Tag: noindex, so they are read, not indexed. /api/knowledge (the
# public Knowledge Catalog JSON) sends no noindex and may be indexed, like the
# public API routes above. "Allow: /api/mcp$" matches only the exact path,
# i.e. the keyless GET discovery document. The agent-readiness probe and the
# payment options read are advertised by llms.txt and the agent-payments guide.
Allow: /api/v1/sandbox/fixtures
Allow: /api/v1/errors
Allow: /api/knowledge
Allow: /api/mcp$
Allow: /api/v1/health/agent-readiness
Allow: /api/v1/payments/options
Disallow: /api/

# Named AI-crawler groups below intentionally restate the SAME Allow/Disallow
# policy as User-agent: *. A crawler obeys only its single most-specific
# matching group and does NOT inherit the * group, so the /api/ disallow
